{{More citations needed|date=March 2026}}{{Short description|Ukrainian mathematician}}
'''Volodymyr Levytskyi''' was a Ukrainian mathematician who was the first to publish a mathematical paper in Ukrainian, doing so in 1894. He earned a doctorate in 1901 at [[University of Lviv|Lviv University]] under [[Józef Puzyna]]. Like fellow Ukrainian [[Mykola Chaikovskyi]], Levytskyi worked in Lviv and in high schools. Unlike Chaikovskyi, he maintained close contacts with the Polish [[Lwów School of Mathematics]] and published many papers on [[Analytic function|analytic functions]] in German.<ref name="zusmanovich">{{cite journal
 | last = Zusmanovich | first = Pasha
 | doi = 10.5642/jhummath.EGCM7534
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Humanistic Mathematics
 | mr = 4758663
 | pages = 114–167
 | title = Mathematicians going east
 | volume = 14
 | year = 2024| doi-access = free
 }} See in particular pages 141–142.</ref> 

In 1929, [[Mykhailo Kravchuk]] encouraged Levytskyi to emigrate to Ukraine, offering positions either in Kyiv or in Kharkiv, but nothing came out of these efforts. Levytskyi repeatedly denounced the Soviet regime in public. In 1932, he resigned his membership in the Kyiv mathematical society to protest its politicization, which included dismissal of [[Dmytro Grave]] as its head. He later resigned from the Soviet Ukrainian Academy of Sciences as well.<ref name="zusmanovich" />

Upon Russian occupation of Lviv in 1939, and its subsequent Ukrainization, Levytskyi was appointed as a professor at the Lviv University. After [[World War II]], upon the exodus of Polish mathematicians, he occupied the chair of [[Stefan Banach]] and tried to preserve what little remained of the traditions of the Lwów School of Mathematics. He died peacefully in 1956.<ref name="zusmanovich" />
